 Judgment

Dated this the 5th day of November, 2025 The petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.250 of 2013 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Neyyattinkara, has preferred this appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the tribunal on account of the injuries sustained by him in a motor accident that occurred on 12.08.2012.
2.

The case of the petitioner, in brief, is as follows :-
On 12.08.2012, while the petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-19-A- 8021 ridden by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner along Udiyankulangara - Vlathankara public road, and when the motorcycle reached near Vattavila Junction, on seeing a KSRTC bus coming from the opposite direction, the 1 st respondent abruptly turned the motorcycle towards the left side without reducing the speed.
As the 1 st respondent turned the motorcycle abruptly in a negligent manner, the petitioner was thrown on to the road and sustained serious injuries.
3. The owner cum rider of the offending motorcycle was arrayed as the 1st respondent, whereas, the insurer was arrayed 2025:KER:84276 as the 2 nd respondent.
The 2 nd respondent contested the petition and filed a written statement mainly disputing the quantum of compensation claimed.
However, the 2 nd respondent admitted the insurance coverage of the motorcycle involved in the accident.
4. During trial, documents produced from the side of the petitioner were marked as Exts.A1 to A17.
From the side of the respondent, Exts.B1 to B3 were marked.

5. After trial, the tribunal came to the conclusion that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-19-A-8021 by the 1st respondent, and being the insurer, the 2nd respondent was held liable to pay the compensation.
The compensation was quantified at Rs.1,45,440/-, rounded to Rs.1,46,000/- with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till realisation and proportionate costs.
Dissatisfied with the compensation awarded by the tribunal, the petitioner has come up with this appeal.

6. I heard Sri.S. Nikhil Sankar, learned counsel appearing for the appellant and Sri.Lal K. Joseph,
learned counsel for the 2nd respondent, insurance company.

Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the compensation awarded by the tribunal under various heads, particularly, under the head of permanent disability, is too meagre and is not sufficient to compensate the actual loss and damages incurred by the petitioner due to the accident.

Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent, insurance company, would submit that the R.Udayakumar vs Ratheesh Kumar on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121636514/
2
compensation awarded by the tribunal under each and every head is just, fair, reasonable and adequate and hence, no interference is warranted.
8. From the rival contentions raised, it is discernible that the main dispute that revolves around this appeal is with respect to the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal.

A perusal of the impugned award reveals that, for the purpose of determining compensation under the head of permanent disability and loss of earnings, the tribunal assessed the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.6,000/-.
In the petition, it is averred that the petitioner was working as a Mason at the time of the accident and was earning a monthly income of Rs.15,000/-.

Apart from raising such an averment in the petition, no documents, whatsoever, was produced from the side of the petitioner to substantiate his averments regarding 2025:KER:84276 his avocation or income.
Any how, the accident occurred in the year 2012.

Therefore, having regard to the year of the accident and by applying the principles laid down by the Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd. [(2011) 13 SCC 236], the tribunal ought to have assessed the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.8,500/.
9.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd. [(2011) 13 SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to prove that the petitioner had suffered permanent disability due to the injuries sustained in the accident, a disability certificate issued by a doctor was produced and marked in evidence as Ext.A10.
In Ext.A10 disability certificate, it is recorded that the petitioner had suffered a disability of 18%.
However, the tribunal, without assigning any convincing reason, scaled down the disability to 6%, while computing the compensation under the head of permanent disability.

I am of the considered view that, if at all the tribunal was having any doubt regarding the reliability of disability certificate issued by the doctor, the course open for it was to refer the petitioner for examination by a competent medical board.
However, instead of doing so, the tribunal abruptly scaled down the disability to 6%.
Moreover, as per the 2025:KER:84276 treatment records, it is evident that the injuries sustained by the petitioner include fracture of left tibia.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
In the disability certificate, which is marked as Ext.A8, it is specifically stated that the fracture of tibia remains malunited even at the time of examination.
Likewise, in the disability certificate, it is mentioned that there is a shortening of left leg 1 cm.
Considering the above, I am of the view that the tribunal ought to have acted upon the percentage of disability noted in the disability certificate while computing the compensation.
Admittedly, the petitioner was aged 28 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, in view of the decision in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [2010 (2) KLT 802 (SC)], the multiplier applicable in his case is 17.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [2010 (2) KLT 802 (SC)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Resultantly, the petitioner is found entitled to get an amount of Rs.3,12,120/- (8,500/- x 12 x 17 x 18/100) as compensation under the head of permanent disability.
Already an amount of Rs.73,440/- has been awarded by the tribunal under the said head.
After deducting the said amount, the petitioner is found entitled to get an amount of Rs.2,38,680/- as additional compensation under the head of permanent disability.
Consequent to the revision in the monthly income, necessary enhancement has to be made in the compensation awarded under the head of loss of earnings.
Moreover, the tribunal awarded compensation under the said head only for a period of two months.

Given the nature of injuries R.Udayakumar vs Ratheesh Kumar on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121636514/
3 sustained by the petitioner
, I am of the view that the petitioner would have been prevented from doing any work or earning income at least for a period of ten months.
Hence, the petitioner is found entitled to get an amount of Rs.85,000/- (8,500/- x 10) as compensation under the head of loss of earnings.

After deducting the amount of compensation already awarded under the said head, the petitioner is entitled to get an amount of Rs.73,000/- as additional compensation under the head of loss of earnings.
11. Moreover, the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner speaks for itself regarding the pain and suffering endured by him due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
Therefore, the same has to be compensated adequately.
The tribunal already awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- as compensation under the said head.
The said compensation awarded by the tribunal under the said head appears to be on 2025:KER:84276 the lower side.

Considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the treatment procedures undergone by him, I am of the view that an additional amount of Rs.50,000/- has to be awarded under the head of pain and suffering as well.

12. Likewise, the hardships and inconveniences met by the petitioner due to the injuries sustained in the accident also cannot be overlooked while awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities and enjoyment in life.
Already an amount of Rs.24,500/- has been awarded by the tribunal under the said head.

I am of the view that an amount of Rs.50,000/- has to be awarded as compensation under the head of loss of amenities and enjoyment in life, entitling the petitioner to get an additional compensation of Rs.25,500/- under the said head.
13. The compensation awarded by the tribunal under other heads appears to be reasonable and justifiable, and interference is unwarranted in respect of those heads.
Hence, an amount of Rs.3,87,180/- (Rs.2,38,680/- + Rs.73,000/- + Rs.50,000/- + Rs.25,500/-) has to be added towards the total compensation awarded by the tribunal.

In the light of the aforesaid observations and findings, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of Rs.3,87,180/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Eighty Seven Thousand One Hundred and Eighty only) with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum on the enhanced compensation from the date of claim petition till the date of deposit, after deducting interest for a period of 240 days, i.e., the period of delay in preferring this appeal and as directed by this Court on 16.07.2025 in C.M. Appln. No.1/2020.

The respondent insurance company is ordered to deposit the enhanced compensation with interest before the tribunal with proportionate costs,
within a period of three months from the date of this judgment.

Immediately on the compensation amount being deposited, the tribunal shall, after deducting the liability of the appellant/petitioner towards court fee, disburse the compensation amount to the appellant/petitioner in accordance with law.

Sd/-
JOBIN SEBASTIAN JUDGE Jvt/
